title: Timing of levothyroxine administration affects serum thyrotropin concentration
authors: Bach-Huynh TG, Nayak B, Loh J, Soldin S, Jonklaas J
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
population: Patients at Georgetown University taking levothyroxine for hypothyroidism or thyroid cancer, randomised to six sequences of fasting, bedtime and with-breakfast dosing
funder: This project was conducted through the General Clinical Research Center at Georgetown University and supported by Grant M01-RR-020359 from the National Center for Research Resources (NCRR), NIH. J.J. is supported by NCRR Grant K23 RR16524. S.S. is partially supported by NIH GCRC Grant MO1-RR-020359 and by Applied Biosystems/Sciex.
authorConflicts: The authors have nothing to disclose.
result: Mean TSH was 1.06 (SD 1.23) mIU/l with fasting intake, 2.93 (3.29) with breakfast and 2.19 (2.66) at bedtime; both non-fasting regimens gave significantly higher and more variable TSH. Classified as industry because one author was partially supported by Applied Biosystems/Sciex.
